what_its_for: This medicine helps lower high potassium levels in your blood (a condition called hyperkalemia). Having too much potassium in your blood can cause serious heart problems. This medicine works by trapping extra potassium in your gut so it leaves your body through your stool instead of building up in your blood.
how_to_take: Mix the powder packet with about 3 tablespoons (45 mL) of water. Stir well and drink right away while it is still cloudy. If the powder settles to the bottom, stir again before drinking. You can take this medicine with or without food. Do not swallow the dry powder directly from the packet.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your potassium levels. A common starting dose is one 10-gram packet (one envelope) mixed in water, taken 3 times a day for the first 2 days. After that, your doctor will likely lower your dose to once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on regular blood tests.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, just skip the missed one and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store the sealed packets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep packets in a dry place away from moisture. Do not use a packet if it has been opened or if you can see any damage to the packaging. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Take other oral medications at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking this medicine, because it can affect how your body absorbs other drugs. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid eating foods that are very high in potassium (such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, and tomatoes) unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet (which could be a sign of too much fluid buildup); feel unusually weak or fatigued; notice your heart is beating irregularly; or if your potassium levels seem too low (symptoms include muscle cramps, weakness, or constipation). Also contact your doctor if you develop nausea, vomiting, or any new or worsening symptoms. Seek emergency help immediately if you have chest pain or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working within 1 hour of your first dose to begin lowering potassium levels. Most people see a significant improvement in their potassium levels within the first 24 to 48 hours. Your doctor will check your blood potassium levels regularly to make sure the medicine is working and to adjust your dose as needed.
special_populations: Kidney disease: This medicine is commonly used in people with kidney disease, who are at higher risk for high potassium. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Heart failure: Tell your doctor if you have heart failure, as this medicine contains sodium which could cause your body to retain extra fluid and worsen swelling. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known how this medicine affects unborn babies or infants. Children: The safety and effectiveness of this medicine in children has not been fully established. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but regular monitoring is still important.
